newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom Malaysia posts 19 pct rise in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Telekom Malaysia posts 19 pct rise in 1996 profit.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd on Thursday reported net profit of 1.88 billion ringgit ($758 million) for 1996, a growth of 19.4 percent over 1995 and a shade above market forecasts.
Equity analysts had expected Telekom to announce net earnings of between 1.8 billion and 1.85 billion ringgit, against 1.575 billion for the year ended December 31, 1995.
"It's relatively in line ... nothing really earth-shattering," said a telecommunications analyst at a British brokerage.
The market appeared to agree, with the counter's shares closing unchanged at 19.30 ringgit.
"Sustainability will be the key going forward," the analyst added, noting the growth rate of 19.4 percent compared with 12.6 in the previous year.

Telekom said it was proposing one bonus share for every two existing shares held by shareholders. The planned bonus issue will raise its issued and paid-up share capital to just under three billion ringgit.
The company said despite a slight decrease in employee numbers, individual productivity rose further to 137 lines per employee in 1996 from 116 in 1995.
Its capital expenditure for the year was 2.3 billion ringgit. Telephone revenues accounted for 88.0 percent of total operating revenue compared with 89.9 percent in 1995.
Another telecommunications analyst said trimming the workforce and higher revenue from leased lines may have boosted profits.
The utility firm said its operating revenue was 6.42 billion ringgit for the year ended December 31, 1996, up from 5.25 billion in the previous year.
The higher profit was achieved on the back of "strong and continuous economic growth in Malaysia", the company said in a statement accompanying its financial results.
"The telecommunication environment is becoming competitive and the group is positioning itself to maintain its performance in 1997," it said in a statement.
